summary: Iter 27 — Legal Terms + Privacy gate end-to-end testing. All 11 backend tests pass (status, current, accept happy path, mismatched/unchecked version rejections, register/login include needs_legal_acceptance, force re-acceptance via DB). Frontend gate verified: registration redirects to /accept-terms, both documents render with disabled checkboxes/accept button, scroll-to-bottom enables checkboxes, checking both enables accept, POST /api/legal/accept clears the gate and redirects to /app, reload stays on /app, public /terms and /privacy render, Protected wrapper redirects /app, /billing, /settings, /admin to /accept-terms when needs_legal_acceptance=true, SIGN OUT clears tokens and returns to /, and admin@atlas.app is also gated (needs_legal_acceptance=true on login).
critical_code_review_comments: legal.py — IP capture via x-forwarded-for is good, but no IP validation; IPv6/IPv4 mixed strings are truncated to 64 chars which is fine. Consider also recording user-agent string for stronger audit trail (compliance nicety).

auth.py — `from routes.legal import needs_acceptance` is imported lazily inside login/me to avoid circular imports; this is fine but could be hoisted to module top since legal.py only depends on db/get_current_user via factory; no functional issue.
documents.js — Body markdown contains hard-coded [STATE PLACEHOLDER] and [CITY, STATE] placeholders in section 11 of Terms — flag for legal/product owner to replace before going to production.

AcceptTerms.jsx — Scroll detection requires the user to reach within 8px of the bottom. On very tall viewports the scroll element collapses to its content height and may already be at-bottom; works correctly today because container has fixed h-[440px] on mobile and uses flex on lg.
App.js — Protected wrapper checks `user?.needs_legal_acceptance` but does not check `token` separately for /accept-terms itself (intentionally — AcceptTerms.jsx handles that bounce). OK.

Audit immutability: legal_acceptance is overwritten on each /accept call. For audit compliance, consider appending to a history array (e.g., legal_acceptance_history: [...]) so historical version acceptances are preserved when versions are bumped.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (gate, public pages, sign-out, protected-route redirects, admin gate)

test_credentials: Admin: admin@atlas.app / Open0says3me#*03#* (now requires legal acceptance on next login — verified). Test users created with pattern legaltest_<uuid>@example.com / TestPass123!
seed_data_creation: Created ~5 ephemeral users prefixed legaltest_ via /api/auth/register during the test run. Admin account state: legal_acceptance was NOT applied during testing (admin only logged via API to confirm needs_legal_acceptance=true; admin did NOT complete acceptance through the frontend, so admin will still be gated on next login). All legaltest_* users that completed acceptance now have legal_acceptance set to 2026-02-01.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter 27 legal gate is fully functional and verified. Backend constants live at /app/backend/routes/legal.py (CURRENT_TERMS_VERSION / CURRENT_PRIVACY_VERSION) and MUST be kept in sync with /app/frontend/src/legal/documents.js. Admin account (admin@atlas.app) has NOT yet accepted in the DB — if subsequent iterations need admin access via the UI, the test agent will need to complete the gate flow (scroll both bodies, tick both checkboxes, click I AGREE) OR run a one-time MongoDB update via $set on legal_acceptance.
rca of the issue: N/A — no defects found. All required behaviors verified.
